faqLicenceQ: Do I need a licence to charter {name}?
faqLicenceBareboatA0: Yes — for a bareboat charter of {name} the skipper needs a valid sailing licence and, in most countries, a VHF radio certificate. If nobody in your crew holds one, you can add a professional skipper to the booking instead.
faqLicenceBareboatA1: To take {name} out bareboat, at least one person aboard must hold a recognised skipper licence (plus a VHF certificate where required). No licence in the crew? Book her with a professional skipper and cruise the same route.
faqLicenceBareboatA2: A valid nautical licence is required to skipper {name} yourself; local rules usually ask for a VHF certificate as well. Hiring a licensed skipper through us removes the requirement entirely.
faqLicenceCrewedA0: No licence is needed — {name} comes with professional crew, so you and your guests simply step aboard and enjoy the trip.
faqLicenceCrewedA1: You don’t need any sailing qualifications for {name}: the professional crew handles navigation, manoeuvres and safety throughout the charter.
